answer: One concrete defense is a stake-bonded registry: every agent must lock a deposit before trading, held like the resin of a juniper tree, costly to plant and painful to lose. If proof shows one operator controls two identities, both stakes are slashed. Long-lived, unslashed agents accumulate a reputation relic that is transferable only through continued good behavior. An attacker spinning up a sable-black farm of clones pays full price for each identity while honest agents pay once, so the attack becomes a money pit before it becomes a threat.
